text.en:
Kabir came home from cricket with muddy hands. He reached for a biscuit.
"Stop!" said Amma. "What do we do first?"
"Wash my hands with soap!" said Kabir. He had almost forgotten.

Germs are tiny living things we cannot see. Some of them make us ill.
Washing hands with soap and water removes germs. Wash before eating and after using the toilet or playing outside.
Brush the teeth twice a day: in the morning and at night.
Bathe every day, cut nails, wear clean clothes, and sleep enough.
These habits keep us healthy and happy.
Germs are so small that we cannot see them. Some can make us ill.
Wash your hands with soap before eating and after playing or using the toilet.
Brush your teeth in the morning and at night. Bathe every day.
Clean habits keep the body healthy, and a healthy body is a happy one.

problem.en: Kabir's hands are muddy and he wants to eat. What should he do first, and why?

text.en: Wash his hands with soap and water.

why.en: Soap and water remove mud and germs.

text.en: Rub them well, front and back, between the fingers.

why.en: Clean hands keep germs out of our mouths.

prompt.en: Your younger sister says she can eat without washing hands, because the mud is dry. What will you tell her?

requiredIdeas.en: Germs are too small to see.
Wash hands with soap and water before eating.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking hands are clean if no mud can be seen.

points.en: Wash hands with soap before eating and after playing or using the toilet.
Brush teeth twice a day, bathe every day.
